comparator.name: Artificial Intelligence
comparator.sourceNotes: The English full-time degree combines 120 EC of common courses, a 15 EC specialisation, a 15 EC project and an approved 30 EC minor. This example uses Computational Neuroscience, the first named specialisation in the regulations. Cognitive Neuroscience is listed for introduction from 2027–2028.
components: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence and Cognitive Science

core: Artificial-intelligence foundations, programming, algorithms, logic, mathematics and statistics
Machine learning, data analysis, neural networks and computational optimisation
Autonomous intelligent systems, agents, robotics and decision-making
Human intelligence, cognition, neuroscience and human-centred or hybrid intelligent systems
Language, computational linguistics and natural-language processing
Ethics and philosophy of artificial intelligence and cognition
Scientific methods, communication and independent artificial-intelligence project work
questions: How intelligence can be understood, modelled and designed in humans and machines

routeSelection.basis: Computational Neuroscience is first in the adopted regulations. The Fall 2026 entrant reaches year three in 2028–2029, after the stated introduction of Cognitive Neuroscience. The third-year requirements are based on the entrant regulations, with future term scheduling subject to the catalogue.

selection.assessment: The options prioritise broad AI and autonomous systems, computational machine learning, or cognition and neuroscience. They differ by 45, 52.5 and 90 EC each way. Language and robotics remain evidenced directions beyond the three-option maximum.

alternatives.label: Artificial Intelligence, Cognition and Autonomous Systems
alternatives.labelReason: Programming, calculus, linear algebra and cognitive foundations support machine learning, robotics and probabilistic decision-making.
alternatives.concept: Study how intelligent systems sense, learn and act. Combine programming, algorithms and machine learning with robotics, human cognition and AI ethics.
progression: Programming, calculus, linear algebra and cognitive foundations support machine learning, robotics and probabilistic decision-making.

alternatives.label: Machine Learning and Computational AI
alternatives.labelReason: Programming and mathematics support algorithms, numerical methods and machine learning before neural networks and reinforcement learning.
alternatives.distinctness: Software, computing infrastructure, advanced algorithms and mathematical modelling receive greater weight.
alternatives.concept: Study how machine-learning systems are built and evaluated. Combine algorithms, software development and numerical methods with computer vision, optimisation, neural networks and reinforcement learning.
progression: Programming and mathematics support algorithms, numerical methods and machine learning before neural networks and reinforcement learning.

alternatives.label: Cognition, Neuroscience and AI
alternatives.labelReason: Brain and behaviour and neurobiology support perception and higher cognitive functions. Research design and statistics support evidence synthesis, while programming and mathematics support machine learning.
alternatives.distinctness: Brain, perception, language, human development and cognitive research receive greater weight.
alternatives.concept: Study how brains perceive, learn and process language, alongside computational models of learning and decision-making. Combine neurobiology, cognitive psychology, research methods and AI.
progression: Brain and behaviour and neurobiology support perception and higher cognitive functions. Research design and statistics support evidence synthesis, while programming and mathematics support machine learning.

blocks: Both study formal logic, including propositional and predicate reasoning.
Both teach object-oriented design. UCR also teaches functional programming.
Both study data structures, search, sorting and algorithmic complexity.
Both teach programming through functions, control flow and practical problem solving.
Both teach calculus and optimisation. Groningen applies these methods to AI.
Both study matrices, vector spaces and eigenvalues. Groningen also teaches multivariable calculus in this course.
Both study signals, sampling and the behaviour of linear systems.
Both study probability, estimation and statistical inference.
Groningen brings reasoning, agents, perception and language processing together in one course.
Groningen gives students a separate overview of AI as a field.
Groningen continues formal logic in a separate course.
Machine learning, data and autonomous systems
Both model intelligent decisions and agent behaviour. UCR gives particular attention to uncertainty.
Both prepare, analyse and visualise data. Groningen also emphasises communication.
Both teach learning from data, including regression, classification and model validation.
Both study robot movement, sensing and control. UCR focuses on robotics.
Groningen requires a project that takes machine learning from data preparation to model evaluation. UCR applies machine learning in several courses.
Groningen uses computational architectures to model human cognition.
Groningen uses computational tools to model mechanisms of the brain.
Groningen studies computation inspired by neural circuits. UCR’s neural networks course focuses on deep learning.
Both introduce neural systems and the biological basis of behaviour.
Both study learning and cognition. UCR introduces these within a broader course on brain and behaviour.
Groningen teaches general linguistics. UCR’s Psycholinguistics course focuses on how people process language.
Groningen teaches computational processing of text and language. UCR’s Psycholinguistics course focuses on human language processing.
The regulations list this course from 2027–2028. UCR studies cognition and its neural basis in several courses.
Mind, ethics and responsible artificial intelligence
Both examine fairness, accountability and the social effects of AI.
Both study philosophical questions about mind and cognition. Groningen gives greater attention to AI.
Research, project work and open choice
Groningen has a separate scientific skills course. UCR develops research methods across its curriculum.
Groningen requires an AI research project. Independent research at UCR is optional.
Students complete a 30 EC minor or other approved study.

notes.text: Groningen requires dedicated work in computational language processing, advanced logic and computational neuroscience, plus an AI project. UCR offers related courses in programming, machine learning, robotics and cognition.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

audience.programmeDescription: Artificial Intelligence at the University of Groningen combines computing and mathematics with the study of mind, brain and language. This example follows Computational Neuroscience and concludes with a research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines AI, cognition and robotics. The other options emphasise computational methods or the science of human cognition. Groningen has separate courses in natural language processing and brain modelling.
